law_name: Gaza reconstruction programme presented to the Cairo donors' conference (2014)
description: As Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy, Mustafa was put in charge of rebuilding Gaza after the 2014 war and led the PA's ministerial committee at the donors' conference for the reconstruction of Gaza held in Cairo in 2014, according to WAFA.
significance: Reconstruction stalled amid the dispute between Abbas's government and Hamas over control of Gaza and shortfalls in donor funding; Mustafa resigned in March 2015 (see polemics). He was given the same task again in 2024.

description: Presented to President Abbas on 28 March 2024 together with the cabinet list, in response to the letter of designation of 14 March. It names the PLO, its political programme and its international commitments as the government's political reference, and lists as priorities a comprehensive relief plan for Gaza, recovery and reconstruction in Gaza and the West Bank, stabilising the public finances, institutional reform and unification, the fight against corruption, better services, digital transformation, the rule of law, financial-sector integrity, the judiciary, security and public freedoms, and support for Jerusalem, the Jordan Valley and marginalised areas. The cabinet created a Ministry of State for Relief Affairs focused on Gaza and a Ministry of Industry.
significance: In the absence of a functioning Legislative Council, the reply to the letter of designation served as the government's ministerial statement, according to the AMAN Coalition. It framed the PA's response to US and European demands for a 'revitalized' Palestinian Authority.

law_name: National Program for Development and Reform (PA reform agenda agreed with the EU and donors, 2024–2026)
description: Reform programme designed, according to Mustafa, 'in partnership with the European Union, the World Bank, and key donors', and reviewed at the Palestine Donor Group meetings he co-chaired with EU Commissioner Dubravka Šuica in Brussels in November 2025 and July 2026. It covers public financial management (expenditure controls, VAT and tax reform, net lending, local-authority debts), social protection, education modernisation, the merger and dissolution of institutions, anti-corruption, merit-based senior appointments and security leadership. In July 2026 the government reported progress on 53 milestones in four pillars and adopted an 18-month strategy 'from reform to recovery' with five pillars: resilience, institutions and the rule of law, Gaza's recovery and the gradual restoration of government responsibilities there, economic self-reliance, and wider international recognition of the State of Palestine.
significance: The basis of the EU's financial support, including through the PEGASE mechanism, and of the PA's case for a role in Gaza, where the PA's reforms are a condition discussed under the US plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803; independent assessments such as AMAN's 2025 report are mixed (see promises).

law_name: Social protection reform: presidential decree of 10 February 2025 and Decree-Law No. 4 of 2025
description: President Abbas's decree of 10 February 2025 ended payments to prisoners based on the length of their sentence and to families of those killed in the conflict, transferring assistance to the needs-based programme of the Palestinian National Economic Empowerment Institution (Tamkeen). Mustafa's government implements the reform, which he describes as a single, transparent, needs-based social protection framework established under Decree-Law No. 4 of 2025, overseen by an independent supervisory structure and supported by a national registry and digital platform.
significance: A long-standing demand of the United States, Israel and European donors; its implementation is disputed (November 2025 payments under the old system, dismissal of the finance minister, US rejection of the July 2026 audit). See promises and polemics.

description: New local elections law approved by the Council of Ministers in 2025, according to Mustafa, under which the Central Elections Commission organised the local elections of 25 April 2026 in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in the Gaza Strip. According to the AMAN Coalition, amendments to the law required candidates to sign a declaration committing to the PLO's political programme and international obligations.
significance: The first local elections since 2006 to include part of Gaza; the candidate declaration was criticised by civil society and human rights organisations (see polemics).

law_name: Palestinian Authority Liaison Office with the Office of the High Representative for Gaza (2026)
description: Liaison office headed by Mustafa, announced by Vice-President Hussein al-Sheikh in a letter to Nickolay Mladenov on 21 February 2026, as 'a clear and organized channel for coordination and communication' on the US 20-point plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803. In April 2026 Mustafa added a specialised committee in the Prime Minister's Office to coordinate with the High Representative and prepare the transfer of Gaza's administration to the PA at the end of the transitional phase.
significance: The PA's formal channel into the post-war arrangements for Gaza, whose day-to-day administration was given to a technocratic committee without PA members.
